changes.before: This attributes the sources separately and avoids inventing causation. A exaggerates, C combines incompatible numbers, and D assumes contradiction where none exists. Next step: Write a synthesis using “while” or “however” and a limitation.
changes.after: The supported synthesis attributes the sources separately and avoids inventing causation. The trial does not establish that every travel problem was solved or that all parents agreed. changes.before: C integrates both sources with appropriate caution. A and D claim unmeasured outcomes; B ignores the 73 reported benefits and potential overlap. Next step: Use an evidence-plus-limitation sentence.

Guaranteed examination gains and one-to-one counting across the data sets are not established. The claim that nobody gained study time ignores the 73 respondents reporting a benefit and possible overlap between response categories. Next step: Use an evidence-plus-limitation sentence.
